_comment: Per-stop sky (DeepSky.h). 'band' changes the Milky Way itself: view (center / anticenter / outward), light colours, gas grown inside the band (cloud, cloudAccent, clouds, cloudReach), dust, angle/offset/width/intensityScale. 'skyPaint' puts the ship inside soft lit clouds; 'planet' moves/scales/hides the backdrop planet; 'stars' and 'motes' scale the star count and the near dust. 'objects' are large soft nebulae, haze, clusters, galaxies and belts, rendered inside the band so its dust crosses them. Authored with the backdrop planet top right; a mirrored stop mirrors everything. Stops 0-5 keep the plain sky; 6-15 light, 16-29 medium, 30-41 strong, 42-49 the Galactic Centre. 'orbit' makes the stop a low orbit around one of its planets (planet index, optional kind override): the planet becomes a horizon arc at one screen edge and the whole sky turns past it as one panorama, so the band and the host star set behind it; an orbit stop draws no objects, nebula, skyPaint or asteroids. 'framing': 'disk' instead shows the whole planet at the screen centre (diskRadius) seen from a higher orbit: its phase follows the star, which can pass behind it (eclipse). An orbit may add a 'ring' (inner/outer in planet radii, tiltDeg from the orbit plane, nodeDeg; it opens and closes as we orbit) and a 'moon'. 'spin' is the planet's own rotation over the orbit rate: the ground runs (1 - spin) times as fast as the sky (0 = tidally locked, negative = against the orbit). Stops 50-58 (gc-*) are the Galactic Centre tour after Sgr A* (galaxy_centre_tour.json).

hd-147873._note: Looking away from the centre: the anticentre band is faint, thin and icy over a deep black sky.

wispit-2._note: WISPIT 2 is a young star with a protoplanetary disc: the dusty nursery it was born in is still around it.

hat-p-46._note: Lagoon-like: a huge magenta star-forming cloud split by a dark lane.

hat-p-45._note: The game's opening look: soft teal and pink clouds all around the ship.

k2-202._note: Eclipse in an orange haze: the planet slides in front of the host star, whose light spills around its limb.

k2-237._note: On a spiral arm: the band crowded with red H-alpha clouds and blue young clusters.

toi-3474._note: The system's asteroid belt streams across the view, lit by the host star.

toi-3464._note: A Wolf-Rayet wind bubble beside an H-alpha cloud.

ic-4651-9122._note: IC 4651 is a real old open cluster (about 1.7 Gyr): gold and white stars, no young blue haze.

corot-35._note: Above the plane looking outward: the Milky Way sinks to the bottom, the sky above is dark with Andromeda.

kmt-2020-blg-0414l._note: The host is a white dwarf: the cast-off shells of its death drift around the system.

moa-2010-blg-477l._note: Deep space: the line of sight leaves the plane, the Milky Way is a faint glow below, few stars, a couple of distant galaxies.

kmt-2019-blg-1216l._note: Carina-like giant star-forming complex: gold and rose glow with dark pillars rising into it.

ogle-2012-blg-0026l._note: Deep inside a rose emission cloud: one pink hue fills the whole view, very close.

ogle-2019-blg-0468l._note: A rogue planet with no star drifts as a dark silhouette in front of a supernova remnant's shock filaments.

kmt-2021-blg-0171l._note: Deep inside an amber dust cloud: one warm hue fills the whole view, very close.

kmt-2022-blg-1818l._note: Deep in the dusty inner disk: amber starlight torn by heavy dark lanes, almost no gas.

kmt-2024-blg-0404l._note: Seen edge-on from just inside the thin disk, the Milky Way is a thin bright line; the planet sits dead centre and hides part of it.

route-37._note: Crab-like pulsar wind nebula: blue synchrotron glow caged in red filaments.

route-38._note: A dense asteroid belt close by, under a yellow-lit sky.

route-39._note: Inside a violet-lit cloud: one hue, full screen, close.

route-40._note: Rosette-like: a hollow rose-orange nebula carved by the young blue cluster in its middle.

route-41._note: Inside a crimson cloud: one deep red hue, full screen, close.

route-42._note: First sight of the Fermi bubbles rising out of the plane ahead.

route-43._note: Galactic Centre region: violet synchrotron-lit gas and cyan hot clouds, threaded by the radio arc.

route-44._note: Inside Sgr B2, the densest molecular cloud of the Galaxy: dark red murk with knots of newborn-star H-alpha.

route-45._note: Arches cluster: the densest young cluster known, blue-white, inside teal-lit gas.

route-46._note: Quintuplet cluster and the Pistol star's LBV bubble in a red-lit region.

route-47._note: Between the Fermi bubbles: two giant lobes stand above and below the plane.

route-48._note: Near the centre: violet-brown dust and a few newborn-star glows, in the manner of stop 43.

route-49._note: Inside the nuclear star cluster around Sgr A*: the densest crowd of stars in the Galaxy fills the sky with gold light.

sgr-a-star._note: The climax: a closer, wider band behind a bigger black hole.

gj-680._note: A different angle: the Milky Way arches across the upper sky, as a wide-field view sees it.

hd-136352._note: The hot zone, with our own character: neon-warm like Hotline Miami, glowing out of deep violet dark like Animal Well. Hot pink flanks, gold core, orange-red gas with yellow hearts, black-violet dust lanes, and sunset-ramp clouds right around the ship.

gc-ringed-giant._note: Galactic Centre tour: a ringed gas giant seen whole from a high orbit; the rings open and close as we go round.

gc-eclipse._note: The host star slides behind an ocean world: a thin crescent, then only the lit ring of its atmosphere, then sunrise.

gc-far-ice._note: A small ice world far below, high above the plane: the sky is the scene.

gc-lava-night._note: The night side of a lava world, its cracks glowing; the star is behind it.

gc-hot-ceiling._note: Upside down: a hot Jupiter fills the top of the screen and the sky falls up into it.

gc-blue-ice-giant._note: An ice giant under a hot blue star, with a thin ring almost edge-on.

gc-moon-transit._note: A desert world and its moon.

gc-ring-arch._note: Low over a ringed giant: the rings rise from the horizon as an arch across the sky.

gc-red-giant._note: A swollen red giant rises over a scorched world; the orbit runs backwards so the sky climbs away from the planet.
